name: multi-account-netlify-mcp

tools.name: netlify-user-services-reader
tools.description:
Select and run one of the following Netlify read operations (read-only) get-user

Multi-account (the account argument): get-user: every named account answers.

account.description: Netlify account to use: one name, several names separated by commas, or "all". Lists and all only work for operations that allow them; changes need one name. Leave out to use the default account. Accounts: none yet.

tools.name: netlify-deploy-services-reader
tools.description:
Select and run one of the following Netlify read operations (read-only) get-deploy, get-deploy-for-site

Multi-account (the account argument): get-deploy: only the account that owns the id answers, and accounts without it are listed under notFoundIn; get-deploy-for-site: only the account that owns the id answers, and accounts without it are listed under notFoundIn.

account.description: Netlify account to use: one name, several names separated by commas, or "all". Lists and all only work for operations that allow them; changes need one name. Leave out to use the default account. Accounts: none yet.

tools.name: netlify-deploy-services-updater
tools.description:
Select and run one of the following Netlify write operations deploy-site

Multi-account (the account argument): deploy-site: one account only, so a list or all is refused.

deployDirectory.description: absolute file path to the directory containing the code that should be deployed. Must be the root of the project repo unless specified.

siteId.description: provide the site id of the site of this site. If the agent cannot find the siteId, the user must confirm this is a new site. NEVER assume the user wants a new site. Use 'netlify link' CLI command to link to an existing site and get a site id.

account.description: Netlify account to use: one name, several names separated by commas, or "all". Lists and all only work for operations that allow them; changes need one name. Leave out to use the default account. Accounts: none yet.

tools.name: netlify-project-services-updater
tools.description:
Select and run one of the following Netlify write operations update-visitor-access-controls, update-forms, manage-form-submissions, update-project-name, manage-env-vars, create-new-project

Multi-account (the account argument): update-visitor-access-controls: one account only, so a list or all is refused; update-forms: one account only, so a list or all is refused; manage-form-submissions: get-submissions needs the account that owns the form (only it answers); delete-submission needs one account; update-project-name: one account only, so a list or all is refused; manage-env-vars: listing needs the account that owns the site (only it answers); creating, updating and deleting need one account; create-new-project: one account only, so a list or all is refused.

from_ts.description: Start timestamp in milliseconds since Unix epoch (not seconds). How far back data goes depends on the team plan (typically 24 hours on free, 7 days on pro and business, 30 days on enterprise). An older start is clamped to that limit, and a window entirely before it fails with "requested window out of bounds".

to_ts.description: End timestamp in milliseconds since Unix epoch (not seconds)

query_name.description: Which dimension to count requests by

filters.description: Filters to narrow the requests. Filters on different fields are ANDed; filters on the same field are ORed. Range operators (>, <, >=, <=) only apply to StatusCode. URL, UserAgent, RequestId, ClientAddress, ConnectionAddress and LogText only accept "=", and LogText matches text within function log lines. Example: [{"field":"StatusCode","op":">=","value":500}]

value.description: A number for StatusCode, a string for everything else
